audit_comment: THE DRAGON ISSUE-20 OPENER PART TWO - the two-chain round of the issue-20 three-round shape. Two chains pinned from the Curtiss-provided Dm20.pdf scan: the Fitzgerald It Is A Good Day To Die - the 600-death Saskatoon wilderness-campaign census, thirty-one causes with the percentage column in tenths; the Sagui Demonic Possession in the Dungeon - the type-IV-or-greater possession doctrine, the amulet rules, the host-death and repossession ladders, the exorcism ritual with the wraith and spectre turning mirrors and the victim outcomes. The closing flip rides R942, closing both report-020 boxes.

banner.title: The Dragon issue-20 opener part two - the 600-death campaign census and the demonic possession doctrine
banner.provenance: The part-two round of the issue-20 three-round shape - the remaining two of the five Curtiss-called chains pinned, after the R940 Polynesian pantheon, witch ladder and demonology grids. All pinned from The Dragon Vol. III No. 6 (November 1978), the Curtiss-provided Dm20.pdf scan voice, print folio the PDF page minus two.
banner.sentinel: The part-two print catches pinned as scanned: the death-census percentage column sums to 100.1 percent not 100 (pinned in tenths, 1001, the conversion noted), the possession victim-freed line prints 55 percent with a dangling dash and a singular point of damage, and the 1-10 freed band prints 1 - 10 spaced. Both inherited watches - the Sullin levels 7-9 and the brawling sequel - print nowhere in TD20 and ride to TD 21.

consts.name: dstDeathPctSumTenths
consts.comment: the percentage column sums to 1001 tenths - 100.1 percent, a print catch pinned as scanned the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstDeathCompileMinYears
consts.comment: the statistics compile window - 2 to 3 years, the floor the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstDeathCompileMaxYears
consts.comment: the statistics compile window - 2 to 3 years, the ceiling the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstDeathEstimate
consts.comment: the all-time death estimate - about a thousand player and hireling deaths in the 4 years the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstMenTypesMinPct
consts.comment: the men-types band floor - assassination, pirates, spells, war and the rest, 20 to 25 percent of all deaths the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstMenTypesMaxPct
consts.comment: the men-types band ceiling - 25 percent, the biggest killers as a class the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstGoblinBandMin
consts.comment: the goblin-types encounter band floor - up to 300 or 400 orcs or goblins the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstGoblinBandMax
consts.comment: the goblin-types encounter band ceiling - 400 of the 300-400 band the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstDeathFiveCauses
consts.comment: the five-death misc causes - liches, suicides and drowning the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstDeathFourCauses
consts.comment: the four-death misc causes - minotaurs, ochre-jelly blobs and stakes in hearts the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstDeathThreeCauses
consts.comment: the three-death misc causes - invisible stalkers, sea monsters, lizard men, harpies, tigers, rockslides, starvation and freezing the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstDeathFactors
consts.comment: the four deadly encounter factors - the creature power, the number likely encountered, the willingness to attack and the meeting frequency the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

consts.name: dstPossessMinType
consts.comment: only demons of type IV or greater and the princes are capable of possessing bodies of adventurers the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstAmuletMileRange
consts.comment: the amulet of the demon must remain on the same plane and world, within one mile of the place of possession the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstPossessPaladinBonus
consts.comment: paladins and clerics get a plus one on the possession saving throw the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstPossessPrincePenalty
consts.comment: princes cause a minus two on the possession saving throw the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstHostDeathRepossessPct
consts.comment: at the death of the host body the demon has a 20 percent chance to possess the killer, unless a lawful cleric or paladin the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstPostDeathStaySpiritPct
consts.comment: the post-death stay-as-spirit outcome - 35 percent, not attacking the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstPostDeathBodyPlanePct
consts.comment: the post-death transport-to-body-plane outcome - 35 percent, staying there the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstPostDeathBodyFightPct
consts.comment: the post-death body-to-the-room outcome - 30 percent, continuing the fight in earnest the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstRaisedRepossessPct
consts.comment: if the victim is raised after the death there is a 10 percent chance of the demon repossessing the body after the save versus death ray the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstExorcismPrepRounds
consts.comment: the exorcism needs two rounds of preparation with no fighting before the first attempt the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstExorcismEveryRounds
consts.comment: the cleric may attempt an exorcism every five rounds after the preparation the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstExorcismClericHpMin
consts.comment: each exorcism attempt costs the cleric 1-6 hit points - the floor the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstExorcismClericHpMax
consts.comment: each exorcism attempt costs the cleric 1-6 hit points - the ceiling the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstVictimFreedPct
consts.comment: the exorcised victim is freed 55 percent of the time - the dangling-dash print catch rides this line the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstVictimFreedDmgMin
consts.comment: the freed victim takes 1-10 points of damage - the floor the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstVictimFreedDmgMax
consts.comment: the freed victim takes 1-10 points of damage - the ceiling the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstVictimInsanePct
consts.comment: the exorcised victim goes insane 25 percent of the time, treated in the usual ways the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstVictimDeadPct
consts.comment: the exorcised victim drops dead 20 percent of the time, revival may be attempted the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstRemoveCurseDemonLevel
consts.comment: against remove curse or limited wish the demon saves as a thirteenth level cleric versus death ray the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstFullWishDemonLevel
consts.comment: against a full wish the demon saves as a ninth level cleric versus dragon breath the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstPrinceSaveBonus
consts.comment: princes get a plus two on the remove curse, limited wish and full wish saves the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstSubdueStrFloor
consts.comment: the possessed may be subdued only by two or more fighters of strength at least 18(01) - the strength floor the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstSubdueStrRoll
consts.comment: the subdual strength roll floor - 18(01), the exceptional-strength 01 the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

consts.name: dstSubdueFighterCount
consts.comment: the subdual needs two or more qualifying fighters the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstWildernessCampaign
bools.comment: the campaign is primarily a wilderness one, as the statistics reflect, though huge dungeons exist the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

bools.name: dstPlayersAndHirelingsOnly
bools.comment: the 600 deaths are playing characters and their advanceable hirelings, not mercenaries or other non-playing characters the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

bools.name: dstPatriarchsNoDeaths
bools.comment: patriarchs caused no deaths - you meet them as often as evil high priests but they will not attack, the willingness factor the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

bools.name: dstSurpriseWorstHazard
bools.comment: the worst thing is to be surprised, even by a minor creature - even badly outgunned you can usually escape with enough warning the death statistics census (print 26, PDF 28)

bools.name: dstTwoPlaneRuleOfThumb
bools.comment: the rule of the thumb - only demons immune to all but magical weapons exist upon two planes at once and may possess, the body sent to another plane while the spiritual essence remains the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstRandomVictim
bools.comment: the demon should be placed by the DM but the victim must be at random - first in, last in, fourth or whatever - to preserve fair play the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstOnePerBody
bools.comment: only one demon will inhabit a body at one time and only one member will be possessed in one party at one time the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstKeepsVictimAc
bools.comment: the possessed member has the same armor class as the victim before possession the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstAnyWeaponExceptLawful
bools.comment: the possessed may use any weapon except those aligned Lawful, regardless of previous character class the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstAttacksAsDemonLevel
bools.comment: the possessed attack with those weapons as whatever level demon they are, not the level of the victim the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstKeepsPowersExceptGate
bools.comment: the demon retains all powers while possessing except the ability to gate the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstNoFlightWithoutWings
bools.comment: nothing precluded by the new shape - no physical flight without wings, no Balrog immolation the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstHostTakesDamage
bools.comment: all hits and damage are taken by the infested body rather than the demon itself the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstDetectEvilRegisters
bools.comment: the possessed registers on Detect Evil or reacts violently to Holy Water, paladins with their power to detect recognize possession immediately the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstDropsAlignedGear
bools.comment: one of the first give-away actions is divesting all aligned weapons or equipment the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstNoAlignmentShock
bools.comment: the victims lose no points to alignment shock but feel intense pain in the presence of aligned weapons the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstBreaksRopesLeather
bools.comment: restraint is almost impossible - the possessed break all rope and leather restraints and all but the strongest chains the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstPrincesNotSubdued
bools.comment: demon princes may not be subdued the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstNoChaosBlame
bools.comment: the actions of a person while possessed are controlled by the demon so no chaotic action will be held against them the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstDemonsTurnAsWraiths
bools.comment: the exorcism ability is in direct proportion to turning undead - regular demons are rolled for as wraiths the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstPrincesTurnAsSpectres
bools.comment: demon princes are rolled for as a spectre on the turning tables the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstExorcisedNoRepossession
bools.comment: if the demon is driven from the body by exorcism there can be no repossession the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstAmuletHolderImmune
bools.comment: demons cannot possess a person who is in control of his amulet the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstAmuletContactInstantDeath
bools.comment: if a once-possessed person comes in contact with the possessing demon amulet it causes instant death the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstAmuletCommandNoDamage
bools.comment: an exorcism by the found amulet, correctly phrased, orders the demon back to its body with no damage to the victim the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstNoTreasureInRoom
bools.comment: there is no treasure in the room in which the possession takes place - the wealth is deposited upon the plane with the corporeal body the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)

bools.name: dstDanglingDashPrintCatch
bools.comment: the victim-freed line prints 55 percent with a dangling dash and a singular point of damage - pinned as scanned, the conversion noted the demonic possession doctrine (print 32, PDF 34)
